source_review.notes: Reviewed all twelve references for identity, edition or date, and claim scope. Publisher and bibliographic records confirmed Kleppmann, Gray-Reuter, Sadalage-Fowler, Bernstein-Newcomer, and Kimball-Caserta. The CIDR archive confirms Helland's 2007 position paper and its explicit assumptions. Fowler's maintained Evolutionary Database Design and Parallel Change pages were checked on 2026-09-06. Official PostgreSQL documentation identified version 18 as current, described exported snapshots and logical change replay, warned that crash recovery can resend changes, and assigned duplicate safety to clients. Current Apache Kafka design documentation was checked for the boundary around transactional Kafka processing and external destinations. The official ISO record identifies ISO 8000-61:2016 edition 1 as published and confirmed in 2022.

evidence: Reviewed definitions of stable key set, scoped log position, snapshot, delta interval, transformation, idempotent application, source and target versions, reconciliation sets, semantic invariants, epoch, replay horizon, arrival rate, application rate, and lag before use.
Checked half-open interval, fold, function application, set difference, empty-set, cardinality, derivative, inequalities, and rate units for consistent operands and renderable delimiters.
Confirmed an empty snapshot-delta gap, key completeness, semantic readiness, capacity convergence, and authority are distinct obligations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Log positions and ordering are scoped to their source guarantee; the notation does not assume a universal global order.

evidence: Executed the versioned migration example and independently traced active a:15@13 and c:30@10, tombstone b@14, one repeated event identity, two stale states, and high-water mark 14.
Recomputed Example and Exercise capacity cases: 2400-2000 gives 400 changes per second of growing lag; 1000-700 gives 300 per second of drain; 90000/300 gives 300 seconds or five minutes.
Recomputed the 650-per-second destination case as 700-650 = 50 changes per second of growing lag and therefore no finite catch-up time under constant continuing rates.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The rate calculations intentionally omit bursts, checkpoint overhead, failures, and validation, all of which the text identifies as additional production evidence needs.

evidence: Verified snapshot plus every transformed committed delta through the cut yields the intended cut state only under the stated consistency, completeness, semantic, order, and idempotency premises.
Verified dL/dt = rho - mu implies nondecreasing lag for mu less than or equal to rho and decreasing lag at rate mu-rho only while mu exceeds rho.
Verified a versioned tombstone defeats any later-arriving state with an older version under the same atomic conditional-application rule.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The derivations establish bounded consequences of stated premises and do not prove a tool, workload, or migration universally correct.

evidence: Reviewed empty and moving snapshots, capture gaps, repeated messages, out-of-order keys, hard deletes, late backfill, ambiguous local times, null and default collapse, numeric overflow and rounding, orphan references, and destination conflicts.

Reviewed hot partitions, huge tenants, log-retention exhaustion, lag divergence, foreground-resource contention, failed checkpoints, direct credentials, queued stale work, incompatible rollback, hidden readers, and disaster restoration.
Reviewed archival, financial, credit, health, privacy, accessibility, cultural, legal-hold, regulator, and public-service cases with explicit qualified-authority limits.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Sensitive and regulated outcomes are not inferred from internal technical checks.

evidence: Traced stable identity, lineage, terminal outcome, one writer, gap-free snapshot and capture, replay safety, scoped ordering, semantic preservation, unmatched evidence, fencing, sensitive-data lifecycle, recovery, and retirement across the migration states.
Confirmed backfill and CDC arbitration compares and writes source versions atomically and retains deletion versions until older input cannot arrive.
Confirmed read cutover, write cutover, state reversibility, and source retirement have separate gates.
invariant_checking.notes: The recommended default is one write authority plus captured propagation; unavoidable dual writes receive explicit stronger obligations.

evidence: Reviewed the snapshot-plus-delta argument and confirmed every premise named in the conclusion is stated rather than assumed from a copy tool.
Reviewed version monotonicity for the atomicity premise and confirmed the deletion case requires a comparable tombstone version.
Reviewed the capacity derivation for consistent change-per-second units and its restriction to sustained rates.
proof_review.notes: Arguments show necessity or conditional sufficiency for bounded mechanisms, not full migration safety.

evidence: Audited uses of consistent, complete, correct, exact, authoritative, idempotent, atomic, guaranteed, safe, current, rollback, readiness, and retirement for premises and scope.
Confirmed row counts, hashes, source agreement, tool success, backup presence, low lag, and local snippet execution are each denied conclusions they cannot establish.
Confirmed PostgreSQL and Kafka behavior is presented as versioned implementation evidence rather than a universal migration guarantee.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No internal review, standard, or implementation mechanism is presented as external approval.

evidence: Executed snippet apply-versioned-migration with the repository verifier under Python 3.14.4.
Observed exit status 0, exact active and tombstone lists, duplicates=1, stale=2, high_watermark=14, and empty standard error.
Confirmed all row-count, order, credit, appointment, deletion, ledger, throughput, archive, and production migration cases are explicitly hypothetical.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The execution validates one finite in-memory transition only and does not reproduce database concurrency, crash recovery, capture, or external effects.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed migration outcome, data-surface inventory, semantic contract, movement modes, snapshot boundary, restartable backfill, CDC joining, capture guarantees, idempotency, expand-migrate-contract evolution, identity, relationships, time, numeric representation, deletion, retention, dual-write limits, multi-layer reconciliation, repair, cutover, rollback, rehearsal, operation, and retirement as one coherent architecture treatment.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed failure and recovery across source logs, slots, chunks, transform versions, checkpoints, retries, skew, queues, deletes, indexes, constraints, direct writers, routing, credentials, backups, sensitive copies, reconciliation stores, operators, support paths, consumers, and retirement. The chapter supplies concrete stop, replay, repair, fence, and evidence decisions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate and professional depth, a formal snapshot-delta model, capacity derivation, six named invariants, eighteen distinct misconceptions, one reproducible versioned replay, ten varied examples with explicit conclusions, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar national-archive transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks, structural validation, symbolic conditions, finite arithmetic, hypothetical examples, and one local Python execution do not validate an external migration, prove database atomicity or capture completeness, establish statistical representativeness, guarantee recovery or data quality, authorize data processing, or provide archival, cultural, financial, clinical, policy, legal, privacy, accessibility, security, compliance, labor, procurement, records, or regulatory approval.
